# Batch B010 (part 1) — skills: code-review, custom-settings

C wf010.review-independent OL WF-010 MUST ;; Review is independent and read-only (no edits or rewrites unless asked); code-review is the canonical procedure that the code-reviewer agent and other workflows reference instead of redefining criteria. ;; = ;; Edits when asked. ;;
C wf011.priorities OL WF-011 MUST ;; Prioritize findings: correctness, security/authorization, data integrity/persistence, architecture boundaries, concurrency/integration, meaningful test gaps, maintainability, credible evidenced performance. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf011.no-style-over-defects OL WF-011 MUST_NOT ;; Do not elevate style preferences above behavioural defects or bury important findings under them. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf010.review-scope OL WF-010,WF-001 MUST ;; Establish what is reviewed (files, working diff, branch/PR, feature) and read changed code plus enough surrounding code (callers, contracts, dependencies); do not review isolated lines. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf010.review-intent OL WF-010 MUST ;; Identify the behaviour added/changed, expected error cases, persistence/external effects and the tests protecting it. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf001.review-read-rules OL WF-001 MUST ;; Read the rules whose paths match the changed files and load specialised technique skills only where relevant. ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov001.review-spec-contract OL GOV-001,GOV-008 MUST ;; In review, a non-empty SPECIFICATION.md is the authoritative product contract and approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md values are intended behaviour. ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov003.review-conformance OL GOV-003,GOV-006 MUST ;; Review specification conformance both ways: missing/weakened behaviour and unapproved product behaviour (new limits, reserved values, required fields, workflow restrictions, validation rules, string-comparison semantics incl. DB collation or framework defaults when the spec is silent). ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov005.review-approved-details OL GOV-005,GOV-004,GOV-007 MUST ;; An explicitly approved and synchronized detail absent from the original spec is not a defect; do not confuse internal implementation details with product behaviour. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf012.concrete-correctness OL WF-012,WF-011 MUST ;; Look for concrete behavioural problems with a plausible execution path (conditions, edge cases, async, cancellation, error mapping, lifetimes, side effects, races); do not invent hypothetical failures. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf011.review-architecture OL WF-011,ARC-001,ARC-008,ARC-010,ARC-013,ARC-014,ARC-016,ARC-020,GOV-012 MUST ;; Check backend changes against architecture.md: Domain independence, Application free of Infrastructure/EF, thin Controllers, specific repositories with EF inside Infrastructure, UoW commit boundary, proportional design without unapproved consequential patterns. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf012.no-require-unadopted OL WF-012,WF-011,ARC-009 MUST_NOT ;; Do not report violations merely for differing from unadopted patterns and do not require MediatR, CQRS, VSA, Minimal APIs, Rich Domain Models, Domain Events or generic repositories. ;; = ;; none ;;
C fe.review-frontend OL FE-003,FE-006,FE-007,FE-009,FE-012,SEC-005,FE-002 MUST ;; Check Angular changes against angular.md (feature boundaries, data-access boundary, subscription lifetime, error handling, guards not server authorization, unnecessary global state, meaningful frontend tests); do not mechanically apply backend project-boundary rules to Angular. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf011.review-data-security OL WF-011,SEC-004,SEC-003,SEC-010,PST-008,PST-010,RUN-021 MUST ;; Review data-access and security-sensitive code: transactions/commits, destructive changes, raw SQL parameterization, authorization, trust boundaries, secrets, sensitive logging, concurrency, migrations, cache consistency, and DbSeeder updates when seeded entities are affected. ;; = ;; When relevant. ;;
C wf007.security-scan-risk-scoped OL WF-007,WF-020 MUST ;; Normal security review of changed code is part of every review; run full security-scan only on request, for materially security-sensitive changes or a concrete finding; not every review is a full OWASP audit. ;; = ;; none ;;
C run016.review-integrations OL RUN-003,RUN-015,RUN-016,RUN-005 MUST ;; For external calls check cancellation, timeouts, idempotency, retry safety, failure translation and disposal/lifetime; do not demand retries for operations unsafe to retry. ;; = ;; none ;;
C tst.review-tests OL TST-009,TST-010,TST-011,TST-003 MUST ;; Check that changed behaviour has useful maintained coverage (behaviour not line count), regression tests for plausible-recurrence bugs, preserved probes; do not request duplicate tests. ;; = ;; Equivalent coverage exists. ;;
C wf011.credible-performance OL WF-011,RUN-008 MUST ;; Report performance concerns only when credible (N+1, unbounded materialization, repeated expensive calls, blocking async, demonstrated hot-path allocation); do not recommend speculative optimizations. ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf021.review-tooling OL WF-021,WF-012 MUST ;; Use available diagnostics/analyzers as evidence; no MCP server or analyzer is required; read the code before turning a tool warning into a finding. ;; = ;; none ;;
C x.cr-output-format EX WF-011 MUST ;; Report findings ordered by severity with severity, file/location, what is wrong, why it matters and smallest fix, using the Critical/High/Medium/Low scale as defined. ;; = ;; none ;; The findings format and four-level severity scale are candidate output-shape rules not in the oracle.
C wf012.no-invented-findings OL WF-012 MUST_NOT ;; Do not invent findings to populate categories; when none are meaningful say so and state important unverifiable areas. ;; = ;; none ;;
C x.cr-no-filler-praise EX WF-012 MUST_NOT ;; Do not add filler praise to balance criticism. ;; = ;; none ;; Output-tone restriction not stated in WF-012.
C wf011.review-discipline OL WF-011,WF-010,WF-012 MUST_NOT ;; During review do not rewrite working code unless asked, report tooling-owned formatting as a defect, demand personal style, assume every warning is a bug, or require patterns the project has not adopted. ;; = ;; none ;;

@@ output/template/.claude/skills/custom-settings/SKILL.md ;; Workflow skill routed from CLAUDE.md and reminded by file-change hook.
@scope workflow custom-settings (CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value added/changed/removed/applied/reviewed)
1-7 IM ;; Frontmatter: name and trigger description.
9 NN ;; Ownership/scope/loading banner.
11 NN ;; Heading.
13-19 OL [gov009.resolve-first,gov011.framework-defaults-not-settings,wf001.cs-read-rules]
21 NN ;; Heading.
23-24 OL [gov008.record-setting]
25-26 MX [gov021.update-owning,x.cs-single-source] ;; Updating code/validation/config is GOV-021; preferring one normal source over duplicating the literal is additional.
27 OL [gov021.update-owning]
28-29 OL [gov021.update-owning]
31 NN ;; Heading.
33-36 OL [gov021.propagate]
38-47 OL [gov021.search-list]
49-50 OL [gov021.only-affected]
52 NN ;; Heading.
54-63 OL [pst009.db-impact]
65 NN ;; Heading.
67-69 OL [fe010.settings-sync]
71 NN ;; Heading.
73-78 OL [gov021.verification]
80 OL [gov021.propagate] ;; ;; Do not declare the setting synchronized merely because one constant changed.

C gov009.resolve-first OL GOV-009 MUST ;; Resolve any SPECIFICATION/CUSTOM_SETTINGS conflict before changing implementation. ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov011.framework-defaults-not-settings OL GOV-011,GOV-008 MUST_NOT ;; Framework defaults the project has not intentionally overridden are not settings (not recorded in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md). ;; = ;; none ;;
C wf001.cs-read-rules OL WF-001 MUST ;; Before editing an affected surface read the rules whose paths match it (persistence.md/architecture.md for persistence metadata, angular.md for frontend validation). ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov008.record-setting OL GOV-008 MUST ;; After approval record the setting in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md with a stable descriptive name, value and purpose. ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov021.update-owning OL GOV-021 MUST ;; Update owning code, validation, configuration, tests and externally relevant documentation for a new setting. ;; = ;; Documentation only when externally relevant. ;;
C x.cs-single-source EX GOV-021,GOV-012 PREFER ;; Prefer one normal source in code or configuration over duplicating a setting's literal across layers. ;; = ;; none ;; Single-source design preference not stated in GOV-021.
C gov021.propagate OL GOV-021 MUST ;; When an approved value is added/changed/removed update every affected implementation, validation, configuration, test, documentation and mirrored frontend/backend surface; one changed literal does not establish synchronization. ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov021.search-list OL GOV-021 MUST ;; Search for the old value/name, validators/DTO constraints, Domain/Application checks, DB mapping constraints, frontend validation/UI hints, tests/test data, documentation/examples and mirroring configuration. ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov021.only-affected OL GOV-021,GOV-014 MUST ;; Separate occurrences expressing the setting from numeric coincidences and update only affected behaviour. ;; = ;; none ;;
C pst009.db-impact OL PST-009 MUST ;; When a settings change affects schema metadata update EF mapping, create the appropriate migration per workflow (edit/regenerate only uncommitted migrations when normal; never casually alter existing ones), verify seeding validity, update provider-sensitive tests when relevant. ;; = ;; none ;;
C fe010.settings-sync OL FE-010,GOV-021 MUST ;; When frontend and backend expose the same constraint backend validation stays authoritative and frontend validation/messages stay synchronized. ;; = ;; none ;;
C gov021.verification OL GOV-021,GOV-009,WF-003 MUST ;; Verify settings changes: search stale references, build affected projects, run relevant tests, verify persistence, check SPECIFICATION.md for conflicts, run verify. ;; = ;; none ;;
